default.title: Try Python
default.instructions: Write some Python code and click Run.

debug01.title: Debug 1
debug01.instructions: This function should add 1 to a number and print 5. Run the code, read any error, and fix the mistake.
debug01.hint: Check the punctuation at the end of the function definition.

debug02.title: Debug 2
debug02.instructions: This function should subtract 2 from 8 and print 6. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug02.hint: Check which arithmetic operation the function uses.

debug03.title: Debug 3
debug03.instructions: This function should return True for 5 and print True. Run the code and fix the error.
debug03.code:
def is_positive(number):
    if number > 0
        return True
    return False

print(is_positive(5))
debug03.hint: An if statement needs punctuation at the end of its first line.

debug04.title: Debug 4
debug04.instructions: This function should add two numbers and print 9. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug04.hint: Does the function combine the numbers by adding or multiplying them?

debug05.title: Debug 5
debug05.instructions: This function should add 3 to 4 and print 7. Run the code and fix the error.
debug05.hint: Check that every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket.

debug06.title: Debug 6
debug06.instructions: This function should return True for the even number 8. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug06.hint: What remainder should an even number have when divided by 2?

debug07.title: Debug 7
debug07.instructions: This function should double 6 and print 12. Run the code and fix the error.
debug07.hint: The return keyword is followed by the value to send back, not an assignment.

debug08.title: Debug 8
debug08.instructions: This function should print 'Hello, Ava'. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug08.hint: The function receives a name. Check whether its return value uses that input.

debug09.title: Debug 9
debug09.instructions: This function should print the words Good morning. Run the code and fix the error.
debug09.hint: Check that the text starts and ends with a matching quote.

debug10.title: Debug 10
debug10.instructions: This function should return the larger of 3 and 7, so it should print 7. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug10.hint: Check which value is returned when the first number is smaller.

debug11.title: Debug 11
debug11.instructions: This function should square 3 and print 9. Run the code and fix the error.
debug11.hint: Python variable names cannot begin with a number.

debug12.title: Debug 12
debug12.instructions: This function should return the last digit of 47 and print 7. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug12.hint: Think about which arithmetic operator gives the remainder after dividing by 10.

debug13.title: Debug 13
debug13.instructions: This function should double 4 and print 8. Run the code and fix the error.
debug13.hint: The function body needs to be indented beneath its definition.

debug14.title: Debug 14
debug14.instructions: This function should turn 5 into -5 and print -5. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug14.hint: The function should change the sign of a positive number.

debug15.title: Debug 15
debug15.instructions: This function should triple 4 and print 12. Run the code and fix the error.
debug15.hint: Look at the end of the return expression. Is the multiplication complete?

debug16.title: Debug 16
debug16.instructions: A person who is 18 is an adult. This function should print True for 18. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug16.hint: The comparison should include someone whose age is exactly 18.

debug17.title: Debug 17
debug17.instructions: This function should return True for 0 and print True. Run the code and fix the error.
debug17.hint: An if statement checks whether two values are equal; it does not assign a value.

debug18.title: Debug 18
debug18.instructions: This function should subtract 3 from 10 and print 7. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug18.hint: Check whether the function uses the operation named in its name.

debug19.title: Debug 19
debug19.instructions: This function should square 5 and print 25. Run the code and fix the error.
debug19.hint: The exponent operator needs a power value after it.

debug20.title: Debug 20
debug20.instructions: This function should return the smaller of 3 and 7, so it should print 3. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug20.hint: Check which value is returned when the first number is bigger.

debug21.title: Debug 21
debug21.instructions: This function should add the numbers from 1 to 4 and print 10. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug21.hint: Check the stopping value in range. Does the loop include n?

debug22.title: Debug 22
debug22.instructions: This function should count the even numbers in the list and print 2. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug22.hint: An even number has a remainder of 0 when divided by 2.

debug23.title: Debug 23
debug23.instructions: This function should count the positive numbers in the list and print 3. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug23.hint: The number 1 is positive too. Check the boundary in the condition.

debug24.title: Debug 24
debug24.instructions: This function should return the larger of 8 and 3, so it should print 8. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug24.hint: When the condition is true, which number is actually larger?

debug25.title: Debug 25
debug25.instructions: This function should count words longer than 3 letters and print 2. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug25.hint: Compare the number in the condition with the instruction's word length.

debug26.title: Debug 26
debug26.instructions: This function should add only the positive numbers and print 7. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug26.hint: Check the condition that decides which numbers are added to the total.

debug27.title: Debug 27
debug27.instructions: This function should check whether the list contains a zero and print True. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug27.hint: The function is named for the value it needs to find. Check the value in the condition.

debug28.title: Debug 28
debug28.instructions: This function should repeat the word 'hi' three times and print hihihi. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug28.hint: Check how many times the loop runs when times is 3.

debug29.title: Debug 29
debug29.instructions: This function should make a string of 4 stars and print ****. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug29.hint: The loop repeats the right number of times. Check which character it adds.

debug30.title: Debug 30
debug30.instructions: This function should calculate the average of 2, 4, and 6 and print 4. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug30.hint: An average is the total divided by the number of items.

debug31.title: Debug 31
debug31.instructions: This function should describe 0 degrees as Freezing. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug31.hint: Check whether the first condition already includes 0.

debug32.title: Debug 32
debug32.instructions: A score of 50 is a pass. This function should print Pass for 50. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug32.hint: The pass mark itself should count. Check the comparison at the boundary.

debug33.title: Debug 33
debug33.instructions: This function should add 4 and 2 and print 6. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug33.hint: Look at the operation used in the branch for 'add'.

debug34.title: Debug 34
debug34.instructions: This function should count words with 3 or fewer letters and print 2. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug34.hint: The instructions say 3 letters or fewer. Does the condition include a word of length 3?

debug35.title: Debug 35
debug35.instructions: This function should return the smallest number in the list and print 2. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug35.hint: When should the saved smallest value be replaced: when a number is bigger or smaller?

debug36.title: Debug 36
debug36.instructions: This function should count numbers greater than 5 and print 1. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug36.hint: The instruction says greater than 5, not 5 or greater.

debug37.title: Debug 37
debug37.instructions: This function should return the first even number and print 2. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug37.hint: Check the remainder that identifies an even number.

debug38.title: Debug 38
debug38.instructions: This function should multiply the numbers in the list and print 24. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug38.hint: The starting value is ready for multiplication. Check the operation inside the loop.

debug39.title: Debug 39
debug39.instructions: This function should check whether every number is positive. It should print False for [0, 2]. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug39.hint: Positive numbers are greater than zero. What should happen when a number is exactly zero?

debug40.title: Debug 40
debug40.instructions: This function should add the odd numbers from 1 to 5 and print 9. Run it and fix the mistake.
debug40.hint: Check whether the loop includes the number n.
